source.title: Optimizers Qualitatively Alter Solutions And We Should Leverage This
source.authors: Razvan Pascanu; Clare Lyle; Ionut-Vlad Modoranu; Naima Elosegui Borras; Martin Jaggi; Petar Veličković; A. P. Sarath Chandar; Soham De; James Martens

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on test performance in sequential MNIST learning, extending optimizer comparisons to a continual-learning setting.
record.gate_note: The paper's standard image-classification and language-model generalization comparisons are cited background, not its own results. Its own optimizer comparisons report sequential-task test performance and forgetting; no train-test generalization gaps are measured.
record.test_reason: The study's own experiments compare catastrophic forgetting and representation structure across optimizers, rather than adaptive-versus-SGD generalization under limited tuning. For permuted MNIST, the authors explicitly attribute Shampoo's final test-performance advantage to retaining previous tasks after test-based early stopping. They do not state the AdamW-versus-SGD ordering. The class-incremental experiment compares Adam with Shampoo, without SGD. Background discussions of width, batch size and sharpness supply no new tests of those versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that optimizer choice shapes reachable solutions and can encode inductive biases. Their illustrative experiments associate Shampoo with lower-rank representations and reduced forgetting; their reinterpretation of Power-propagation illustrates inducing sparsity through preconditioning, potentially at the cost of training efficiency.
record.recipe_differences: The paper presents illustrative continual-learning examples rather than the standard benchmark and tuning comparisons described in V4; one experiment uses test-error-based early stopping.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice; Adam learning rate (1e-3 versus 1e-4) in the class-incremental MNIST comparison; sequential task setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Shampoo achieves better final average test performance than SGD and AdamW after sequential permuted-MNIST training; the authors attribute this advantage to less forgetting. Its representations also have lower effective rank.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice can alter representation structure and retention of previously learned tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: On sequential MNIST class pairs, Adam retains high accuracy only on the final pair, whereas Shampoo retains nontrivial accuracy on earlier pairs. Lowering Adam's learning rate does not remove this difference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shampoo can reduce catastrophic forgetting relative to Adam in class-incremental MNIST.

record.problems: The optimizer examples are described as thought experiments rather than a methodological contribution. The displayed results are figure-only in the supplied text, with no exact values or uncertainty estimates stated. The permuted-MNIST comparison uses test-error-based early stopping.
record.rows_left_out: No other own optimizer test-performance results were reported in the supplied text. Cited optimizer-generalization findings were excluded because they are prior work.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error beyond the width required for zero training error; the illustrative model-size comparison does not establish this threshold or training convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD generalization under limited tuning, training-performance comparisons, broader tuning, optimizer switching, decoupled weight-decay recovery and language-model exceptions.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and competing measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Neither extracted verdict is warranted: outperforming SGD with Shampoo cannot support V4's adaptive-method disadvantage, and a specialized setting or unavailable exact plot values alone cannot justify limits_scope. The cannot_determine states concern the named claim versions; they do not deny the explicitly reported forgetting results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

The paper tests optimizers only in sequential MNIST learning, not the listed standard image-classification or language benchmarks. It does not test broader hyperparameter tuning, Adam-to-SGD switching, decoupled weight decay, or word-level language models.

rows.subject: SGD

rows.operation_detail: Train sequentially on three different permutations of MNIST using SGD; evaluate average test error across tasks at the end of training.

conditions.value: early stopping based on test error for each task
same initialization across the three algorithms

rows.measure: Average test error on all tasks at the end of training
rows.note: The text says Shampoo outperforms SGD and AdamW; numeric values are shown only in the figure. Early stopping uses test performance.
rows.check: Final sequential-task performance measures retention here; it does not establish V4's optimizer generalization comparison. SGD-versus-AdamW ordering is unavailable. Figure 3's caption calls the measure test accuracy, whereas the prose calls it test error; resolve this before recording a numeric value. The subject is an optimizer, not a model.

rows.note: The text explicitly says Shampoo is outperforming the others. The result concerns sequential-task test performance and forgetting, not a measured train-test gap.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Train on pairs of MNIST digit classes sequentially, one epoch per pair, then evaluate final parameters on each pair's test split.
rows.measure: Accuracy on the test split of each class pair using final trained parameters
rows.note: The text says Adam attains high accuracy only on the final pair; numeric values are in the figure.
rows.check: This measures Adam's forgetting relative to Shampoo, with no SGD comparator. Its partial state cannot describe V4. Figure 4 specifies a 2-layer MLP, which the record omits. The subject is an optimizer, not a model.
